questions.text: The Moon's rotation period is approximately equal to its revolution period around Earth.
Give a reason: We usually see the same face of the Moon from Earth.
questions.answer: Because the Moon's rotation period equals its revolution period around Earth.

questions.text: The changing shapes of the Moon seen from Earth are called Moon ______.

choices: Earth is approximately between the Sun and Moon
Moon is between Sun and Earth
Sun is between Earth and Moon
questions.answer: Earth is approximately between the Sun and Moon

choices: Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
Moon comes between Earth and Sun
Sun comes between Earth and Moon
questions.answer: Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon

questions.text: A lunar eclipse can occur at every full Moon.
Give a reason: A lunar eclipse does not occur every full Moon.
questions.answer: Because the Moon's orbit is tilted, so the Sun, Earth, and Moon are not perfectly aligned every full Moon.

questions.text: The darkest central part of a shadow is called the ______.
The lighter outer part of a shadow is called the ______.
Compare total and partial lunar eclipses.
questions.answer: A total lunar eclipse occurs when the Moon is completely inside Earth's umbra; a partial lunar eclipse occurs when only part of the Moon enters the umbra.

questions.text: Give a reason: The Moon may appear reddish during a total lunar eclipse.
questions.answer: Because some sunlight is refracted and scattered through Earth's atmosphere and reaches the Moon, with red light passing more effectively.
